title: Effect of Vitamin D on MyocardIal Fibrosis in Acute Myocarditis
official: Effect of Vitamin D supplementation on MyocardIal Fibrosis in PaTients with Acute Myocarditis (EDIT-AM): a multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the effect of Vitamin D supplementation on myocardial fibrosis at 6 months follow-up assessed by LGE CMR in patients with uncomplicated AM and low levels of 25OHD
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients admitted with AM aged ≥18 years.
2. Diagnosis confirmed by CMR.
3. Left ventricular ejection fraction ≥40% on CMR.
4. Presence of LGE on CMR
5. 25OHD levels <25 ng/mL
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known allergy or intolerance to calcifediol or its components
2. Dilated, hypertrophic or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
3. Congenital heart disease
4. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or cardiac surgery within the last 3 months
5. Pregnant or lactating women
6. Cancer or any other life-threatening condition
7. Any contraindication to CMR procedures, including allergy or intolerance to gadolinium contrast media
8. Any other medical or physical condition considered unappropriated by a study physician
9. Patients already receiving Vitamin D supplementation
10. Participation in other AM clinical trials
11. Unable to provide written informed consent (either personally or through a designated legal representative) or to provide a contact telephone number.
12. Hypercalcemia (>10.5 mg/dL) or hypercalciuria
13. Calcium nephrolithiasis
14. AM complicated with hemodynamic instability, sustained ventricular tachycardia or new-onset conduction abnormalities
15. Immune checkpoint inhibitors-associated AM
16. Eosinophilic myocarditis
17. Giant Cell myocarditis
18. Granulomatous disorders (tuberculosis, sarcoidosis)
19. Systemic Autoimmune Disorders
